title: (Updated) Microsoft Teams: New centralized experience for organizing important resources in chats and channels
summary: Microsoft Teams will introduce a centralized resource management experience in chats and channels, allowing users to pin and organize resources below headers and access them on mobile. The "In this chat" and "In this channel" panes will be removed. Rollout occurs from late September to mid-November 2026.
body:
Updated October 19, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[What and why]

We are introducing a more consistent way for users to access and manage important resources in Microsoft Teams chats and channels. Users will be able to pin frequently used resources directly below the chat or channel header, pin multiple messages alongside other resources, and organize them into folders. On Microsoft Teams mobile, users will be able to access shared resources and folders by tapping the chat or channel header. This change will help users stay organized and provide them with a centralized location to quickly find, access, and manage important resources.

As part of this update, the In this chat and In this channel panes will be removed. Existing resources within these panes will be accessible through the new resource management experience.

[Rollout schedule]

- Targeted Release (Worldwide): Rollout begins in late September 2026 and is expected to complete by early October 2026.- General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, and DoD): Rollout begins in early November 2026 (previously early October) and is expected to complete by mid-November 2026 (previously mid-October).[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

- Users who access or manage resources in Microsoft Teams chats and channels.Platforms and services

- Microsoft Teams- Microsoft Teams mobileWhat will happen

- Users will have a centralized location to find, access, and manage important resources.- Users will be able to pin frequently used resources directly below the chat or channel header, pin multiple messages alongside other resources, and organize them into folders.- On mobile devices, users will be able to access shared resources and folders by tapping the chat or channel header.- The In this chat and In this channel panes will be removed; existing resources within these panes will be accessed and managed through the updated experience.Screenshot - Comparison before and after

[Action required and recommendations]

No administrative action is required. We recommend that you:

- Inform users about the updated resource pinning and management experience.- Update any internal training or support documentation that references the In this chat and In this channel panes.[Learn more]

We will update this post with new documentation.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
